task.name: Escalation advisor fails to launch, leaving the operator gate with option names and no advice
task.story_text:
## What happened

In sprint run `c23db04fc491` (`issues-1415,2154,2155,2150`, base `release/v0.13`,
2026-08-03), story #1415 reached the escalation gate and the escalation advisor
failed to run at all:

```
08:56:50  Starting openai-gpt-5.4-mini (model=gpt-5.4-mini, timeout=900s)...
08:56:51  ... openai-gpt-5.4-mini done (2s)
08:56:51  WARNING: Codex CLI run for model=gpt-5.4-mini completed cost-unmeasured
          (no token usage in output); recording cost-unknown, NOT $0.00.
08:56:51  [ESCALATION_ADVISOR] FAIL | exit=1 | cost=unknown | output=194 chars
08:56:51  [ESCALATION_ADVISOR] error output: warning: `--full-auto` is deprecated;
          use `--sandbox workspace-write` instead. Reading additional input from
          stdin... Not inside a trusted directory and --skip-git-repo-check was
          not specified.
08:56:51  ⚠ advisor agent returned failure — preserving escalation
```

The advisor process exited after two seconds without ever reaching the model. The
resulting operator checkpoint at `.forge/pending/3e4a57be9314.yaml` carries:

```yaml
advisory_unavailable: true
decision_required: true
options: [accept, land_core_defer_edges, redirect, decompose, elevate, defer_or_abandon]
reason: "ESCALATION TIMED OUT — awaiting an operator action selection (no auto-reject).
  ESCALATION — advisory report unavailable; select an action.
  no verdicts
  PASS
  Quorum unmet: 1/3 succeeded < threshold 2; failed: "
```

The same gate on the same story in the previous run (`675e2792fa1b`, 2026-08-02)
produced a full advisory: a recommended action, and for each of six options an
operation, supporting evidence, a risk and a consequence. In this run the
operator is offered the same six option names with no basis for choosing among
them.

The failure is a tool-invocation error in the environment the advisor is launched
into, not a model or prompt failure. It reproduces on every escalation in the
run, so no escalation in this sprint can produce advice. It is also recorded as
`cost=unknown` rather than as a launch failure that consumed nothing.

## What was expected

An advisory exists to inform a decision a person is about to make, so when it
cannot be produced, the reason it could not be produced is the most useful thing
the run can offer in its place. A failure to launch is a different condition from
an investigation that ran and reached no conclusion, and an operator reading the
checkpoint should be able to tell which occurred and whether it is worth
retrying.

An agent that a run depends on should be launched into an environment where it
can start; where that environment is not established, the run should surface the
launch failure as a defect in its own configuration rather than degrading the
operator to an unaided choice as though advice had merely been unavailable this
time. A process that exits before performing any billable work should be recorded
as having spent nothing, distinctly from work whose cost could not be measured.

## Diagnosis

**Baseline:** `991e2bd5ed378c8978049ebc58fb4449e9424db7` captured at `2026-08-04T02:51:23.279311+00:00`

**Inspected files:**

- `src/theforge/coordinator/escalation_advisor_flow.py` — `sha256:ae164294136a5dcf887204ed2c33680edd1e552469924f64ea59967d0b3e568c`
- `src/theforge/coordinator/preflight_flow.py` — `sha256:35750002e281081d91f99f9a37586325c3fcc0b79a59420e61b6f4cfc77ab763`
- `src/theforge/runners/runner_codex.py` — `sha256:43ca5ac5cb2e18e404f4321dd4dc78e52a3d6a45c4fcb977221b1cbc1a6be3c8`
- `src/theforge/config/bridge.py` — `sha256:c9b383943a9516040ef75a533b9ffaba4a525a13673b8e5757c1bde922a5d8a5`
- `src/theforge/coordinator/model_profiles_bridge.py` — `sha256:c9f59cd7e93d57d60ef0c8da94b0367a5e906657c756d3928c32b7f19ee2772c`
- `forge.yaml` — `sha256:6303b66f213228feed437452aa793214271fbeaf4eafd42eabe2bd71e13304b3`
- `.forge/logs/issues-1415,2154,2155,2150/run-c23db04fc491.log` — `sha256:6707a4d7f38e72451862acd819745fdb8b9df3a97cb93c606cb11bdf6d174199`
- `.forge/logs/issues-2030,2029,2129,1906,1880,1415,728,727/run-675e2792fa1b.log` — `sha256:b7293648c42a1fd4357db0c4fb11e5ac3353e18952f330ffb3bf7beb379de029`

### Observed symptom

On escalation, the "fresh context" advisor agent is supposed to produce an
advisory report (recommendation + per-option risk/consequence analysis) for
the operator's pending-decision checkpoint. In sprint run c23db04fc491,
story #1415's escalation advisor invocation exited after 2 seconds with
exit=1 and no model was ever contacted, so the checkpoint carries only bare
option names with advisory_unavailable: true. The failure is recorded as
cost=unknown even though zero billable work occurred.

### Reproduction / evidence

Run log .forge/logs/issues-1415,2154,2155,2150/run-c23db04fc491.log:537
captures the Codex CLI's own stderr: "Not inside a trusted directory and
--skip-git-repo-check was not specified." Line 531 shows the advisor was
routed to profile "gpt-5.4-mini" (a Codex CLI model). Contrast with the
prior run (.forge/logs/.../run-675e2792fa1b.log:4827), where the same
escalation gate for the same story was routed to profile "sonnet" (Claude,
no such check) and succeeded in 35s with cost=$0.206.

Root mechanism, read directly from HEAD:
- escalation_advisor_flow.py:run_escalation_advisor calls
  `_prepare_preflight_working_dir(config.project_root, config.workspace.base_branch)`
  to build the "clean baseline checkout" the advisor runs against
  (escalation_advisor_flow.py:226-236).
- preflight_flow.py:_prepare_preflight_working_dir (lines 163-195) builds
  that directory via `git archive <base_branch> | tar -x` into a fresh
  tempdir — this produces a plain file tree with NO `.git` directory at all.
- runner_codex.py:build_argv (lines 66-97) constructs the `codex exec`
  argv and never passes `--skip-git-repo-check` (confirmed absent from the
  entire codebase — no reference to it anywhere in src/ or tests/).
- Codex CLI's own trust gate refuses to operate in a directory it cannot
  verify as a recognized git repository unless that flag is passed, so the
  process exits immediately, before ever reaching the model — hence 2s
  wall-clock and no `turn.completed` usage event for `_extract_codex_cost`
  to price, which is why cost lands as `unknown` (correctly, per that
  function's own "never fabricate $0.00" contract) rather than as the
  distinct "$0.00, never started" case this issue asks for.
- Both `run_escalation_advisor` and the ordinary preflight call site
  (preflight_flow.py:296-311) share the identical `_prepare_preflight_working_dir`
  baseline-checkout call, and both hand off to `config.preflight_profile`
  — a profile that per-story adaptive routing (assignment.enabled: true
  in forge.yaml) can freely resolve to any enabled model, including a
  Codex CLI one. This run's earlier "Auto-config: dev=gpt-5.4-mini" line
  (run log:1312) shows issue-1415 was in fact routed to Codex models this
  story; the same routing surface feeds preflight/escalation-advisor.

### Hypotheses tested

- **[ruled out]** The advisor's model/prompt failed to produce parseable output (a reasoning/schema-parsing failure).
  - Evidence: The captured stderr is Codex CLI's own trust-gate refusal, emitted before any model call; exit=1 came back in 2s with no turn.completed usage event, and log_agent_result never got model output at all — this is a subprocess launch failure, not a model or parsing failure.
- **[ruled out]** The escalation advisor was simply unavailable due to a rate limit/quota/transient CLI issue this run.
  - Evidence: The stderr text is deterministic and specific to a fixed CLI safety check tied to the working directory's git-repo status, not a transient service error, and is 100% reproducible whenever this profile+working-dir combination recurs.
- **[confirmed]** The baseline working directory `_prepare_preflight_working_dir` builds via `git archive`+`tar` lacks a `.git` directory, and Codex CLI's trust check rejects any working directory it cannot verify as a git repo — with `--skip-git-repo-check` never passed by forge's codex argv builder.
  - Evidence: preflight_flow.py:163-195 shows the archive+tar construction produces no `.git`; runner_codex.py build_argv (66-97) has no `--skip-git-repo-check` flag anywhere; the captured stderr is exactly Codex's documented message for this condition; the prior run's advisor invocation on the same story succeeded only because adaptive routing happened to select `sonnet` (Claude) instead of a Codex model for that role that time.

### Confirmed cause

The escalation advisor's baseline working directory (built by
`_prepare_preflight_working_dir` via `git archive | tar -x`, shared with the
ordinary preflight call site) is a plain file tree with no `.git` directory.
When per-story adaptive routing assigns a Codex CLI model (openai/*, cli
transport) to `config.preflight_profile` — the profile the escalation
advisor always launches with — Codex's own trust gate refuses to run
against that untrusted-looking directory, and forge's codex argv builder
never passes `--skip-git-repo-check` to satisfy it. The process exits in
~2s before contacting the model, so the run fails to launch on every
escalation for the rest of that story/model-routing window, and its
zero-billable-work exit is recorded identically to a genuinely
cost-unmeasurable completed run.

### Affected code path

src/theforge/coordinator/preflight_flow.py:163-195 (_prepare_preflight_working_dir —
git-archive+tar baseline with no .git)
src/theforge/coordinator/escalation_advisor_flow.py:216-268 (run_escalation_advisor —
reuses that baseline dir and config.preflight_profile without regard to CLI transport)
src/theforge/runners/runner_codex.py:66-97 (build_argv — never passes
--skip-git-repo-check)

### Fix-success criterion

An escalation whose advisor is routed to a Codex CLI model, run against the
`_prepare_preflight_working_dir` baseline checkout, must either (a) reach the
model and produce a real advisory report, or (b) if launch genuinely cannot
succeed, the resulting pending checkpoint must distinguish "advisor failed
to launch (environment/tool-invocation defect, zero cost)" from "advisor ran
and produced no usable advice" — with the launch case recorded as a
configuration defect (e.g. surfaced distinctly in logs/audit, not folded
into the same advisory_unavailable path) and with cost recorded as a
measured $0.00 rather than cost-unknown when the process is confirmed to
have exited before any billable turn began.

### Related findings (out of scope)

> These are adjacent problems noticed during investigation. They are **not** the cause of this issue's symptom and are **out of scope for this fix** — triage them separately under the linked issue. Do not implement them as part of this issue.

- The identical git-archive-baseline + missing --skip-git-repo-check defect will also break ordinary PREFLIGHT (not just the escalation advisor) whenever adaptive routing assigns a Codex CLI model to that role — this run only avoided it there by chance of routing.
- _extract_codex_cost's 'never fabricate $0.00' design is correct for genuine unmeasurable output, but has no separate code path for 'process exited before any turn began' (a true zero-cost case) — worth a dedicated launch-failure classification in runner_codex.py/cli.py rather than folding it into the same cost-unknown bucket as an unparseable-but-executed run.

### Notes

This is a subset of TheForge's general "no --skip-git-repo-check anywhere"
gap: ANY role (preflight, escalation advisor, and potentially plan-agent
review — anything using `_prepare_preflight_working_dir`) that adaptive
routing assigns to a Codex CLI model will hit the identical failure. This
run happened to only surface it via the escalation advisor because that is
where the routing landed a Codex model against the archived baseline dir;
the ordinary PREFLIGHT calls in this same run were routed to `sonnet` and
so didn't trip it. A fix scoped only to escalation_advisor_flow.py would
leave the identical failure mode live for plain preflight the next time
routing picks a Codex model there.

plan_review.findings:
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-opus-cli] Step 2 lists runner_codex.py, runners/api.py and runners/cli.py, but the result type that would carry a launch-failure signal is AgentResult in src/theforge/agent_types.py — which already has a startup_failure: bool field documented as 'True when the agent couldn't start at all', plus failure_code: str | None.
  Suggestion: Prefer reusing the existing startup_failure / failure_code fields on AgentResult rather than adding a new one; if a new field is genuinely needed, edit src/theforge/agent_types.py (not listed in the plan's file set).
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-opus-cli] Step 3 routes the new signal through escalation_advisor_flow.py, but run_escalation_advisor (escalation_advisor_flow.py:252-256) currently collapses every failure into state.advisory_generated = False; return None, and the checkpoint branch in pending_hitl.py:145-147 keys only off advisory is not None and advisory.ok. There is no channel today for 'launch failure' to reach the checkpoint writer.
  Suggestion: Thread the distinction via a state field (e.g. state.advisory_launch_failure / launch reason from result.output or stderr) set before returning None, and branch on it in the pending_hitl else-path so the extra/reason differ from plain advisory_unavailable.
- [P2] [anthropic-opus-cli] Step 4's test paths do not exist: there is no tests/runners/ or tests/coordinator/ directory. Actual files are tests/test_runner_codex.py, tests/test_escalation_advisor.py, tests/test_coord_escalation_advisor.py. Additionally tests/contract/test_codex_cli_contract.py exercises runner_codex.build_argv in four places and will need updating for the new flag.
  Suggestion: Target the flat tests/ layout and include tests/contract/test_codex_cli_contract.py in the argv-change coverage.
- [P2] [google-gemini-3.5-flash-api] The plan references test paths like tests/runners/test_runner_codex.py and tests/coordinator/test_escalation_advisor_flow.py, but the actual test files are located directly under tests/ (e.g., tests/test_runner_codex.py and tests/test_coord_escalation_advisor.py). Suggestion: The dev agent should locate and modify the existing test files directly under the tests/ directory.

soft: Coordinator is pure Python — no LLM calls for routing or process decisions
Schema validation is the integrity boundary — do not relax cross-validation rules
Keep modules single-purpose; extract instead of growing monolith files
Keep pure-data types in low-dependency modules with stdlib-only imports
Separate prompt construction, output parsing, and coordinator control flow

When adding or modifying data that flows between coordinator phases, instrument the change so the actual values are visible in the audit trail — diagnosing sprint failures requires tracing real data, not reconstructing it
Do not create files outside src/, tests/, or docs/. If you need a scratch file for exploration, delete it before committing.

Changes that affect coordinator phase boundaries, state handoff between phases, or adaptive routing/config propagation must include seam-level integration tests covering the touched boundary. Unit tests alone are insufficient when correctness depends on cross-phase state flow.
